attempts.summary: Set up a loopback-backed Btrfs filesystem on node1 with /srv/data mounted as a Btrfs subvolume (fstab-persisted loop + bind mounts), populated baseline application data, took a read-only Btrfs snapshot, modified /srv/data (deleted/corrupted/added files), and restored it by deleting the live subvolume and re-snapshotting from the baseline — restored content matched the baseline byte-for-byte via SHA-256 comparison. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, issued a non-blocking reboot, polled until the node came back, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified the Btrfs mounts, subvolume structure, and /srv/data contents (checksums matching the original baseline) all recovered automatically thanks to the fstab entries.
